newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-SURPRISE PACKAGE BRANN BERGEN INTO LAST EIGHT IN EUROPE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SURPRISE PACKAGE BRANN BERGEN INTO LAST EIGHT IN EUROPE.

text.p: Norway's Brann Bergen completed a a major surprise on Thursday, drawing 2-2 away against the might of PSV Eindhoven to reach the European Cup Winners' Cup quarter-finals 4-3 on aggregate.
PSV, trailing 2-1 from the first leg, failed to capitalise on a host of chances in front of their home crowd and the Norwegians went 2-0 up with goals from their only two real breaks.
Geir Hasund scored in the 35th minute from a cross by Tore Andre Flo and Flo himself in the 59th finished a fine solo effort with a chip over keeper Ronald Waterreus.
Icelandic counterpart Birkir Kristinsson, forecast as likely to be the the weakest link in Brann's defence, probably played the match of his life, making several brilliant saves.
It was Brann defender Geirmund Brendesether who helped PSV's Rene Eykelkamp to finally beat Kristinsson when they both slid the ball over the line to make it 2-1.

Seven minutes before time Boudewijn Zenden shot home the equaliser but it was too little too late for the Dutch league leaders, who ironically have scored 15 goals in their last two home league matches.
